topic: Driving Sustainable Innovation in the Polymer Field: Leadership Perspectives from a Former MGMT Chair
title: Driving Sustainable Innovation in the Polymer Field: Leadership Perspectives from a Former MGMT Chair
session_title: Leadership and Management of Sustainable Solutions in Industry
abstract: Sustainability in the polymer field requires more than scientific breakthroughs—it demands visionary leadership that mobilizes people, resources, and partnerships across academia, industry, and professional societies. This presentation will explore how professionals and leaders can catalyze innovation and enable circular practices by connecting technological advances with organizational capabilities and collaborative networks. Recent progress in biodegradable materials, advanced processing, and waste-reduction strategies demonstrates how innovation happens with cross-functional, aand cross-sector alignment. Drawing on experiences from my involvement in professional societies, I will discuss how these societies can serve as conveners that accelerate sustainable transformation: linking research to production, design to recyclability, and purpose to performance. By highlighting leadership behaviors that foster commitment, persistence and long-term vision, this talk aims to inspire chemical engineers to continue to lead with impact, and create value for both society and the environment through sustainable polymer innovation.

topic: Accelerating the Circular Economy through AI-Powered Material Intelligence
title: Accelerating the Circular Economy through AI-Powered Material Intelligence
session_title: Leadership and Management of Sustainable Solutions in Industry
abstract: As industries push toward net zero goals and circular economy models, one of the most persistent challenges is the lack of data and visibility into the material streams that underpin manufacturing, recycling, and waste management. At Visia, we’re building AI-powered material intelligence systems that give operators real-time insight into the composition, chemistry, and safety of complex secondary materials streams. Our platform combines cutting-edge X-ray imaging with machine learning to identify inbound materials, particularly hazardous ones like lithium-ion batteries, before they enter downstream processes. Inbound analysis not only prevents fires and contamination but also improves resource recovery and operational efficiency across facilities handling electronic, industrial, and municipal waste. This talk will explore the critical role of data in driving sustainability throughout core industrial operations. Drawing on case studies from large-scale deployments, we’ll highlight how industrial leaders can champion digital transformation to meet EPR, ESG, and decarbonization goals. The presentation will also cover best practices to align technical innovation with regulatory frameworks and build scalable partnerships across the circular economy.

topic: From Farm to Fuel: Scaling Biodiversity and Revenue through Anaerobic Digestion in Agri-Tech Systems
title: From Farm to Fuel: Scaling Biodiversity and Revenue through Anaerobic Digestion in Agri-Tech Systems
session_title: Leadership and Management of Sustainable Solutions in Industry
abstract: Global food systems are increasingly vulnerable due to biodiversity loss, which threatens agricultural resilience and productivity. Biodiversity supports essential ecosystem services—from pollination to soil health—that are critical for stable crop yields. Yet, over 50% of U.S. cropland is dedicated to just two crops: corn and soybeans, leading to monoculture-driven soil degradation [1] . Alarmingly, one-third of the fertilizer applied to corn is used merely to compensate for declining soil fertility. This overreliance on synthetic inputs contributes to nutrient runoff, pest vulnerability, and long-term yield instability. To reverse this trend, integrating biodiversity-enhancing practices such as organic fertilization and crop diversification is essential. However, regulatory incentives alone are insufficient; sustainable change requires economically and technical viable solutions. Anaerobic digestion offers a promising circular solution. Globally, over 85 million tons of digestate are produced annually from biogas plants [1] . This nutrient-rich byproduct serves as an organic fertilizer that improves soil structure, enhances microbial biodiversity, and reduces the need for synthetic fertilizers. Digestate-based fertilizers release nutrients more slowly, minimizing leaching and pollution risks while improving water retention and soil health [1] . Simultaneously, the anaerobic digestion process generates renewable biogas, offering farms a dual benefit: reduced waste disposal costs and new revenue streams. This model aligns environmental stewardship with financial sustainability, making it a scalable strategy for regenerative agriculture and an AI-optimized resilient closed loop FARM-to-FUEL Future. References [1] Anaerobic Digestate-Based Fertilizers in Agriculture: Benefits
